treaty_name: Convention between the United Kingdom and the Italian Republic for the avoidance of double taxation with respect to taxes on income and the prevention of fiscal evasion (1988)
eif_quote: The Double Taxation Convention entered into force on 31 December 1990. The convention is effective in Italy from 1 January 1991 and in the UK from: 1 January 1991 for Petroleum Revenue Tax 1 April 1991 for Corporation Tax 6 April 1991 for Income Tax and Capital Gains Tax
source_title: 1988 UK-Italy Double Taxation Convention — in force (gov.uk HTML)

rates.quote: (a) 5 per cent of the gross amount of the dividends if the beneficial owner is a company which controls, directly or indirectly, at least 10 per cent of the voting power in the company paying the dividends;
(b) 15 per cent of the gross amount of the dividends in all other cases.

However, such interest may also be taxed in the Contracting State in which it arises, and according to the laws of that State, but if the recipient is the beneficial owner of the interest the tax so charged shall not exceed 10 per cent of the gross amount of the interest.

However, such royalties may also be taxed in the Contracting State in which they arise and according to the laws of that State, but if the recipient is the beneficial owner of the royalties the tax so charged shall not exceed 8 per cent of the gross amount of the royalties.

ppt.quote: (9) The provisions of this Article shall not apply if the debt-claim in respect of which the interest is paid was created or assigned mainly for the purpose of taking advantage of this Article and not for bona fide commercial reasons.

notes: No general PPT: Italy is not an MLI Party (treaties_merged.json) and the treaty has only specific anti-abuse rules. Dividends: Art. 10(3) states that, as long as UK-resident individuals are entitled under UK law to a dividend tax credit, para. (2) does not apply to UK-source dividends to Italian residents and instead a tax-credit regime applies (UK tax on dividend plus credit capped at 15%, or 5% for 10%+ voting-power companies) — whether UK law still grants such a credit is outside the treaty text and not verified here; the 5%/15% caps of Art. 10(2) are modelled for both directions. Art. 10(9): for holders of 10%+ of a class of shares, treaty relief is denied for dividends paid out of profits earned 12+ months before the 10% was acquired where the shares have not been held 12 months continuously before declaration (bona fide exception) — not modelled as a holding period. Interest exempt at source (Art. 11(3)-(4)) for credit sales of equipment/goods, interest paid by the source State/subdivisions/local authorities (UK: also agencies/instrumentalities), and loans made/guaranteed/insured by the other State, SACE or UK ECGD. Art. 11(10) denies relief to tax-exempt recipients selling the holding within 3 months. Royalty definition includes equipment rental. valid_from = later of the two States' effective dates (Italy 1 Jan 1991; UK income tax 6 Apr 1991, corporation tax 1 Apr 1991).
unverified: Current operation of Art. 10(3) UK tax-credit regime (depends on UK domestic law) not verified
